Hence if $\mathbf{P}_j(R_j) < \tau$, we define $\mathcal{P}'_j$ by combining $R_j$ with an arbitrary other part $B_j$ of $\mathcal{P}_j$ (which has $\mathbf{P}_j(B_j) \ge \tau$); otherwise we let $\mathcal{P}'_j := \mathcal{P}_j$. Denoting $f'_i := \mathbf{E}(f_i \mid \mathcal{P}'_i \otimes \mathcal{P}_{i+1}')$, we now claim that
\begin{equation} \label{eq:fs-bound}
    \widetilde{f}_i \mathbbm{1}_{R_i^c \times R_{i+1}^c} \le 4 f'_i.
\end{equation}
Both sides are $(\mathcal{P}_i \otimes \mathcal{P}_{i+1})$-measurable, so we must check the inequality in every part $A_i \times A_{i+1}$ of $\mathcal{P}_i \otimes \mathcal{P}_{i+1}$. If $A_i = R_i$ or $A_{i+1} = R_{i+1}$, then the left-hand side vanishes. If $\mathbf{P}_i(R_i) < \tau$ and $A_i = B_i$, then we have 
\[

    =

\]

\[
    f_i\mathbbm{1}_{\widetilde{f}_i >4K} \mathbbm{1}_{R_i^c \times R_{i+1}^c} 
    \le f_i \mathbbm{1}_{f'_i >K}
\]
everywhere, which implies
\begin{equation} \label{eq:edges-third-term}
\begin{aligned}
    ||f_i\mathbbm{1}_{\widetilde{f}_i >4K} \mathbbm{1}_{R_i^c \times R_{i+1}^c}||_{L^1} &\le ||f_i \mathbbm{1}_{f'_i >K}||_{L^1} \le \epsilon/4,
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}

Combining \cref{eq:edges-decomposition,eq:edges-first-term,eq:edges-second-term,eq:edges-third-term} completes our proof in the general case. The statement about equal probability spaces $(X_i, \mathbf{P}_i) = (X, \mathbf{P})$ (where $\mathbf{P}$ is the uniform probability distribution on $X$) follows analogously, using part $(iii)$ of \cref{prop:reduction-to-structure} instead of part $(ii)$ (in this case we have all $\mathcal{P}_i = \mathcal{P}$ and all $R_i = R$). It remains to prove the additional claim that \cref{eq:dense-pairs} can be replaced with
\begin{equation} \label{eq:dense-pairs-1}
    ||f \mathbbm{1}_{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P}' \otimes \mathcal{P}') > K} \mathbbm{1}_{\textnormal{diag}(\mathcal{P}')^c} ||_{L^1} \le \frac{\epsilon}{8},

    2||f||_{S^\infty}\sqrt{\mathbf{P}(R)}
    +
    \sum_{\substack{A \in \mathcal{P} \\ A \neq R}} \mathbf{E}[f \mathbbm{1}_{A \times A}]

    2C \delta +

The pseudorandomness assumption in \cref{cor:relative-k-cycle-removal} is fairly general for the following reasons:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[(1).] Firstly, for any function $\nu : X \times Y \to [0, \infty)$, \cref{eq:cut} and \cref{eq:Schatten-infty} imply that
    \[
        ||\nu - 1||_{\substack{ \\ \square}} 
        =
        \sup_{\substack{A \subset X \\ B \subset Y}}
        |\mathbf{E}[(\nu - 1) \mathbbm{1}_{A \times B}]|
        \le 
        \sup_{\substack{A \subset X \\ B \subset Y}}
        \frac{|\mathbf{E}[(\nu - 1) \mathbbm{1}_{A \times B}]|}{\sqrt{\mathbf{P}_X(A) \mathbf{P}_Y(B)}}
        \le 
        ||\nu - 1||_{S^\infty}.
    \]
    When $|X| = |Y| = n$ and $X, Y$ are equipped with the uniform probability distributions, the second-to-last quantity above is $o(1)$ if and only if $\nu$ is $(1, o(n))$-jumbled (or equivalently, if $p \nu$ is $(p, o(pn))$-jumbled for any $p > 0$), using the terminology from \cite{conlon2014extremal}.
    So our assumption that $||\nu - 1||_{\substack{ \\ \square}} = o(1)$ is strictly weaker than the $(p, o(pn))$-jumbledness of $p\nu$, which is weaker than $||\nu - 1||_{S^\infty} = o(1)$, and much weaker than $||\nu - 1||_{S^4} = o(1)$.
    \item[(2).] Secondly, the conditions $||\nu_i - 1||_{S^4} = o(1)$ are themselves weaker than the linear forms conditions of \cite{conlon2014green,tao2006gaussian}, due to \cref{eq:Schatten-2k}. Importantly, our assumptions about $\nu_{i}$ are \emph{separated}, in the sense that each condition concerns only one of the majorants $\nu_{i}$; by contrast, a linear forms-type condition would also include (among many others) an estimate of the form
    \[
        \mathbf{E}_{x_1,\ldots,x_k} \prod_{i=1}^k \nu_{i}(x_i, x_{i+1}) = 1 + o(1).

This is a slight simplification of the proof of \cite[Lemma 2.4]{conlon2021regularity}, since in our case we know that $|V_j| \ge \tau n$ for each $j$. 

Let $W_j$ be the union of all $V_{j'}$'s with $e_G(V_j, V_{j'}) \ge q|V_j||V_{j'}|$; in particular, $e_G(V_j, W_j) \ge q|V_j||W_j|$. Let us consider the bipartite graph $H_j$ with vertex sets $V_j$ and $W_j^0$, where $W_j^0$ is a copy of $W_j$ (so that $W_j^0 \cap V_j = \varnothing$), and edges induced by the edges of $G$. While $H_j$ is not necessarily isomorphic to a subgraph of $G$ (since we may have $V_j \subset W_j$, in which case the vertices in $V_j$ have copies in $W_j^0$), it is true that every $4$-cycle in $H_j$ induces a $4$-cycle in $G$ (the fact that $G$ is a simple graph causes the right pairs of vertices to be distinct in $V(G)$). Moreover, each $4$-cycle in $G$ corresponds to at most two $4$-cycles in $H_j$, and thus $\textnormal{Inj}(C_4, H_j) \ll \textnormal{Inj}(C_4, G)$. This line of reasoning is implicit in \cite[Lemma 2.4]{conlon2021regularity}.

Now if $e(V_j, W_j) < 4|V_j||W_j|^{1/2} + 4|W_j|$, then we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
    e(V_j, W_j) \le \frac{e(V_j, W_j)^2}{q|V_j||W_j|}
    &\ll 
    \frac{|V_j|^2|W_j| + |W_j|^2}{q|V_j||W_j|}
    =
    \frac{|V_j|}{q} + \frac{|W_j|}{q|V_j|}
    \le 
    \frac{|V_j|}{q} + \frac{1}{q\tau}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Otherwise, \cite[Lemma 2.3]{conlon2021regularity} implies that $e(V_j, W_j)^4 |V_j|^{-2} |W_j|^{-2} \ll \textnormal{Inj}(C_4, H_j) \ll \textnormal{Inj}(C_4, G) = T$ (provided that $W_j$ is nonempty). Thus
\[
    e(V_j, W_j) \ll T^{1/4} |V_j|^{1/2} |W_j|^{1/2} \le T^{1/4} n.
\]
Thus in both cases, we have
\[
    e(V_j, W_j) \ll \frac{|V_j|}{q} + \frac{1}{q\tau} + T^{1/4} n.
\]
Summing over all $j$ (which gives a total of at most $n/(\tau n) = 1/\tau$ terms), we recover the desired bound in \cref{eq:dense-pairs-bound}.

If we only count the `off-diagonal' pairs $(V_j, V_{j'})$ with $j \neq j'$, then we may repeat the same reasoning by replacing $W_j$ with $W_j \setminus V_j$. The difference is that $H_j$ is now isomorphic to a subgraph of $G$, since there are no repeated vertices in $V_j$ and $W_j$; thus we have
\[

\]
and we may use the right-hand side as the parameter $T$.

\label{cor:k-cycle-removal-few-4-cycles}
For any $k \in \mathbf{Z}_{\ge 5}$ and any $\epsilon, C > 0$, there exist $n_0, \delta > 0$ such that the following holds. Let $n \ge n_0$, $p_1, \ldots, p_k \ge n^{-1/2}$, and $G_1, \ldots, G_k$ be $n$-vertex graphs with the same vertex set $V$, such that for each $i$,
\begin{equation} \label{eq:few-4-cycles}
    \textnormal{Inj}(C_4, G_i) \le \delta p_i^4 n^4.
\end{equation}
If additionally
\[
    \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_k \text{ distinct}} \mathbbm{1}_{G_1}(x_1, x_2) \cdots \mathbbm{1}_{G_k}(x_k, x_1) \le \delta p_1 \cdots p_k n^k,
\]
then there exist subgraphs $G_i'$ of $G_i$ with $|E(G_i) \setminus E(G_i')| \le \epsilon p_i n^2$ for each $i$, such that
\[
    \sum_{x_1, \ldots, x_k} \mathbbm{1}_{G_1'}(x_1, x_2) \cdots \mathbbm{1}_{G_k'}(x_k, x_1) = 0.
\]

nodes.statement: Fix k in Z_ge 5 and epsilon > 0, and let n_0, delta, tau > 0 be obtained from crefcor:sparse-k-cycle-removal-graphs with q_1 = cdots = q_k := 4, K a large enough multiple of 1/epsilon, and C a large enough absolute constant. Note that we may always decrease our choice of delta and increase our choice of n_0 (in terms of epsilon and k), without breaking the conclusion of crefcor:sparse-k-cycle-removal-graphs; so for a start, let us take delta le 1 without loss of generality. Now let n ge n_0, p_1, ldots, p_k ge n^-1/2, and G_1, ldots, G_k be graphs with the same vertex set V (of size n), such that textnormalInj(C_4, G_i) le delta p_i^4 n^4. To complete our proof, it suffices to verify that each G_i satisfies the conditions in crefcor:sparse-k-cycle-removal-graphs: item[(i).] One has textnormalHom(C_4, G_i) le C(p_i n)^4; item[(ii).] G_i obeys the dense pairs condition with parts of sizes ge tau n. To verify condition (i), note that crefeq:4-cycle-counts implies \[ textnormalHom(C_4, G) ll n^2 + delta p_i^4 n^4 ll p_i^4 n^4, \] which is enough since we chose C to be a large enough absolute constant. Concerning condition (ii), let V = V_1 cup V_2 cup ldots be a partition into parts of sizes ge tau n. Applying creflem:dense-pairs-1 with q := Kp_i and T = textnormalInj(C_4, G_i) le delta p_i^4 n^4, we find that G_i has at most \[ Oleft(fracnKp_i + frac1Kp_i tau^2 + fracdelta^1/4p_i n^2tau right) \] edges between pairs (V_j, V_j') with e_G(V_j, V_j') ge Kp_i |V_j| |V_j'|. We would like this to be at most equal to epsilon p_i n^2/4, which can be achieved if: item[(1).] K is a large enough multiple of 1/epsilon and p_i^2 n ge 1 (both of which are true); item[(2).] 1/tau^2 le n, which is true provided that we increase the value of n_0 accordingly; item[(3).] delta^1/4/tau is smaller than an absolute multiple of epsilon, which is true provided that we decrease the value of delta accordingly. This completes our proof with (new) values of n_0 and delta depending only on epsilon and k (since K and tau also only depend on epsilon and k).

nodes.statement: Let A := k (2max_i (|a_i| + |b_i|) + 1). We choose n_0, delta_0 > 0 as in crefcor:k-cycle-removal-few-4-cycles, for the same value of k and with epsilon/(4kA^2) in place of epsilon; we set delta := delta_0 / max(epsilon^4, epsilon^k) here. Let n, S be as in the corollary's statement; we may assume without loss of generality that n ge n_0, since the conclusion is trivial for n le n_0 provided that delta < n_0^2-k (due to the |S| diagonal solutions (x_1, y_1) = cdots = (x_k, y_k)). For i in Z/kZ, we define the invertible 2 times 2 matrix \[ M_i := a_i & b_i \\ a_i+1 & b_i+1 \] and the set \[ V_i := [-(|a_i|+|b_i|)n, (|a_i|+|b_i|)n] cap Z. \] Finally, we let V be a disjoint union of all the V_i's (so in particular n_0 le n le |V| le An), and define the (bipartite) graph G_i with vertex set V by \[ mathbbm1_G_i(u, v) := mathbbm1_V_i times V_i+1(u, v)\ mathbbm1_Sleft( M_i^-1 u \\ v right), \] where we identify pairs (x, y) in S with vectors x \\ y . Note that for (x_i, y_i), (x_i+1, y_i+1) in S, we have a_i(x_i+1 - x_i) = b_i(y_i+1 - y_i) iff a_i x_i + b_i y_i = a_i x_i+1 + b_i y_i+1 =: u_i for some u_i in V_i. With this change of variables, the system of equations in crefeq:polygonal-solutions can be rewritten as \[ M_i x_i+1 \\ y_i+1 = u_i \\ u_i+1 , i in Z/kZ, \] so that the number of solutions to crefeq:polygonal-solutions becomes sum_u_1, ldots, u_k in V prod_i=1^k mathbbm1_G_i(u_i, u_i+1); we want to show that this is at least equal to delta |S|^k/n^k. Suppose for the sake of contradiction that this is false, so \[ sum_u_1, ldots, u_k in V prod_i=1^k mathbbm1_G_i(u_i, u_i+1) le fracdelta_0epsilon^k frac|S|^kn^k = delta_0 p_1 cdots p_k n^k le delta_0 p_1 cdots p_k |V|^k, \] where p_1 = cdots = p_k := |S|/(epsilon n^2) ge n^-1/2 (by assumption (i)). Similarly, assumption (ii) implies that for each i, \[ sum_substacku_1, u_2, u_3, u_4 in V \\ u_1 neq u_3,\ u_2 neq u_4 mathbbm1_G_i(u_1, u_2) mathbbm1_G_i(u_3, u_2) mathbbm1_G_i(u_1, u_4) mathbbm1_G_i(u_2, u_4) le fracdelta|S|^4n^4 le fracdelta_0epsilon^4 frac|S|^4n^4 le delta_0 p_i^4 |V|^4, \] which is to say, textnormalInj(C_4, G) le delta_0 p_i^4 |V|^4. By the conclusion of our initial application of crefcor:k-cycle-removal-few-4-cycles, we find that there exist subsets E_i subset V_i times V_i+1 such that \[ sum_u_i, u_i+1 mathbbm1_G_i mathbbm1_E_i^c (u_i, u_i+1) le fracepsilon2kA^2 p_i |V|^2 le fracepsilon n^22k p_i = frac|S|2k \] for each i, and also sum_u_1, ldots, u_k in V prod_i=1^k mathbbm1_E_i(u_i, u_i+1) = 0; in other words, sum_i=1^k mathbbm1_E_i^c(u_i, u_i+1) ge 1 everywhere. To obtain a contradiction, we consider the set \[ T := \(u_1, ldots, u_k) in V_1 times cdots times V_k : M_1^-1 u_1 \\ u_2 = cdots = M_k^-1 u_k \\ u_1 in S \, \] which has natural bijections to S and to the edges of each G_i (through S). We conclude that \[ |S| = |T| &le sum_(u_1, ldots, u_k) in T sum_i=1^k mathbbm1_E_i^c(u_i, u_i+1) \\ &= sum_i=1^k sum_(u_1, ldots, u_k) in T mathbbm1_E_i^c(u_i, u_i+1) \\ &= sum_i=1^k sum_(u_i, u_i+1) in V_i times V_i+1 mathbbm1_G_imathbbm1_E_i^c(u_i, u_i+1) le k frac|S|2k = frac|S|2, \] a contradiction. Thus it must be the case that there are at least delta |S|^k/n^k solutions to crefeq:polygonal-solutions, as we wanted.
nodes.raw_latex:
Let $A := k (2\max_i (|a_i| + |b_i|) + 1)$.
We choose $n_0, \delta_0 > 0$ as in \cref{cor:k-cycle-removal-few-4-cycles}, for the same value of $k$ and with $\epsilon/(4kA^2)$ in place of $\epsilon$; we set $\delta := \delta_0 / \max(\epsilon^4, \epsilon^k)$ here.

Let $n, S$ be as in the corollary's statement; we may assume without loss of generality that $n \ge n_0$, since the conclusion is trivial for $n \le n_0$ provided that $\delta < n_0^{2-k}$ (due to the $|S|$ diagonal solutions $(x_1, y_1) = \cdots = (x_k, y_k)$).

For $i \in \mathbf{Z}/k\mathbf{Z}$, we define the invertible $2 \times 2$ matrix 
\[
    M_i := 
    \begin{pmatrix}
        a_i & b_i \\
        a_{i+1} & b_{i+1}
    \end{pmatrix}
\]
and the set
\[
    V_i := [-(|a_i|+|b_i|)n, (|a_i|+|b_i|)n] \cap \mathbf{Z}.
\]
Finally, we let $V$ be a disjoint union of all the $V_i$'s (so in particular $n_0 \le n \le |V| \le An$), and define the (bipartite) graph $G_i$ with vertex set $V$ by
\[
    \mathbbm{1}_{G_i}(u, v) := \mathbbm{1}_{V_{i} \times V_{i+1}}(u, v)\ \mathbbm{1}_S\left( M_i^{-1}\begin{psmall} u \\ v \end{psmall} \right),
\]
where we identify pairs $(x, y) \in S$ with vectors $\begin{psmall} x \\ y \end{psmall}$. Note that for $(x_i, y_i), (x_{i+1}, y_{i+1}) \in S$, we have $a_i(x_{i+1} - x_i) = b_i(y_{i+1} - y_i)$ iff $a_i x_i + b_i y_i = a_i x_{i+1} + b_i y_{i+1} =: u_i$ for some $u_i \in V_i$. With this change of variables, the system of equations in \cref{eq:polygonal-solutions} can be rewritten as
\[
    M_i \begin{pmatrix} x_{i+1} \\ y_{i+1} \end{pmatrix} = 
    \begin{pmatrix} u_i \\ u_{i+1} \end{pmatrix},
    \qquad i \in \mathbf{Z}/k\mathbf{Z},
\]
so that the number of solutions to \cref{eq:polygonal-solutions} becomes $\sum_{u_1, \ldots, u_k \in V} \prod_{i=1}^k \mathbbm{1}_{G_i}(u_i, u_{i+1})$;
we want to show that this is at least equal to $\delta |S|^k/n^k$. Suppose for the sake of contradiction that this is false, so
\[
    \sum_{u_1, \ldots, u_k \in V} 
    \prod_{i=1}^k \mathbbm{1}_{G_i}(u_i, u_{i+1}) \le 
    \frac{\delta_0}{\epsilon^k} \frac{|S|^k}{n^k}
    =
    \delta_0 p_1 \cdots p_k n^k
    \le \delta_0 p_1 \cdots p_k |V|^k,
\]
where $p_1 = \cdots = p_k := |S|/(\epsilon n^2) \ge n^{-1/2}$ (by assumption $(i)$). Similarly, assumption $(ii)$ implies that for each $i$,
\[
    \sum_{\substack{u_1, u_2, u_3, u_4 \in V \\ u_1 \neq u_3,\ u_2 \neq u_4}} \mathbbm{1}_{G_i}(u_1, u_2) \mathbbm{1}_{G_i}(u_3, u_2) \mathbbm{1}_{G_i}(u_1, u_4) \mathbbm{1}_{G_i}(u_2, u_4) 
    \le \frac{\delta|S|^4}{n^4} \le \frac{\delta_0}{\epsilon^4} \frac{|S|^4}{n^4}
    \le \delta_0 p_i^4 |V|^4,
\]

\label{lem:dense-pairs-2}
Let $2 > \alpha > \beta \ge 1$ and $\mathcal{F}$ be an $(\alpha, \beta)$-quasi-smooth family of bipartite graphs. Also, let $\tau, q > 0$, $G$ be an $\mathcal{F}$-free $n$-vertex graph, and $V_1 \cup V_2 \cup \ldots$ be a partition $V(G)$ into parts with at least $\tau n$ elements each. Then $G$ has at most
\[
    O_{\mathcal{F}}\left(
    \frac{n}{q^{(\alpha-1)/(2-\alpha)}}
    \left(1 + \frac{1}{n^{(\alpha - \beta)/(2 - \alpha)} \tau^{\alpha/(2-\alpha)}}\right)\right)
\]
edges lying between pairs $(V_j, V_{j'})$ with $e(V_j, V_{j'}) \ge q |V_j| |V_j'|$ and $j \neq j'$. If $\mathcal{F}$ only consists of complete bipartite graphs $K_{s,t}$, then one can also include the diagonal pairs $(V_j, V_j)$.

For each $j$, denote by $W_j$ the union of all parts $V_{j'}$ with $e(V_j, V_{j'}) \ge q|V_j||V_{j'}|$ and $j \neq j'$; thus in particular $e(V_j, W_j) \ge q|V_j||W_j|$ and $V_j \cap W_j = \varnothing$. Let $H_j$ be the bipartite subgraph of $G$ with vertex sets $V_j$ and $W_j$, and $e(V_j, W_j)$ edges. Then $H_j$ is also $\mathcal{F}$-free, so by the the quasi-smoothness of $\mathcal{F}$ we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
    e(V_j, W_j) &\ll_{\mathcal{F}} \min(|V_j|, |W_j|) \max(|V_j|, |W_j|)^{\alpha - 1} + \max(|V_j|, |W_j|)^\beta
    \\
    &\le |V_j| |W_j|^{\alpha - 1} + n^\beta,
\end{aligned}
\]
where we used that $\alpha - 1 \in (0, 1)$.
If $W_j$ is nonempty, this further implies that upon setting $\gamma := \frac{1}{2-\alpha}$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
    e(V_j, W_j) &\ll_{\mathcal{F}} \frac{e(V_j, W_j)^\gamma}{q^{\gamma - 1} |V_j|^{\gamma - 1} |W_j|^{\gamma - 1}}
    \\
    &\ll 
    \frac{|V_j|^{\gamma} |W_j|^{\gamma(\alpha-1)} + n^{\gamma \beta}}{q^{\gamma - 1} |V_j|^{\gamma - 1} |W_j|^{\gamma - 1}}
    \le
    \frac{|V_j|}{q^{\gamma - 1}}
    + 
    \frac{n^{\gamma \beta - 2(\gamma - 1)}}{(q\tau^2)^{\gamma - 1}}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Summing over all (at most $1/\tau$) values of $j$ and noting that $\gamma \beta - 2(\gamma - 1) = 1 - (\alpha - \beta)/(2 - \alpha)$, we recover the desired upper bound.

Finally, if $\mathcal{F}$ only consists of complete bipartite graphs, then it is okay to include $V_j$ into $W_j$ (provided that $e(V_j, V_j) \ge q|V_j|^2$). While $H_j$ may not be isomorphic to a subgraph of $G$, it must remain $K_{s,t}$-free for each $K_{s,t} \in \mathcal{F}$ (since the existence of such a $K_{s,t}$ would force all the involved vertices in $V_j$ and $W_j^0$ to originate from distinct vertices in $G$, thus inducing a copy of $K_{s,t}$ in $G$).

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{cor:linear-patterns-generalized-Sidon}
nodes.statement: As noted in the remark above, it suffices to prove an analogous statement for subsets of abelian groups G of order n, where gcd(n, a_1cdots a_k) = 1. Suppose that S subset G has |S| ge epsilon n^1/2, and that for each h neq 0, S contains at most C pairs of the form (x, x+h). If t denotes any integer strictly larger than max(C, 1), this implies that S^2 times t contains no matrix of the form \[ x_1 & x_2 & cdots & x_t \\ x_1 + h & x_2 + h & cdots & x_t + h , \] where x_1, ldots, x_t are distinct. In other words, S is (2, t)-Sidon. The conclusion would now follow from crefcor:linear-patterns-st-Sidon, using s = 2 and q = 4, provided that we can show that \[ ||widehatmathbbm1_S||_4 ll_epsilon,C |S|. \] This is equivalent to a bound for the additive energy of S: \#left\(a, b, c, d) in S^4 : a - b = c - d right\ ll_epsilon,C frac|S|^4n. But we have \[ \#left\(a, b, c, d) in S^4 : a - b = c - d right\ &= sum_h in G \#left\(a, b, c, d) in S^4 : a - b = c - d = hright\ \\ &= sum_h in G left(\#left\(a, b) in S^2 : a - b = h right\right)^2. \] The contribution of h = 0 is exactly |S|^2. Moreover, by our second assumption, the contribution of each h neq 0 is at most C^2. Overall, we obtain \[ \#left\(a, b, c, d) in S^4 : a - b = c - d right\ le |S|^2 + C^2 n, \] which is acceptable in crefeq:additive-energy since |S| ge epsilon n^1/2. This completes our proof.

As noted in the remark above, it suffices to prove an analogous statement for subsets of abelian groups $G$ of order $n$, where $\gcd(n, a_1\cdots a_k) = 1$. Suppose that $S \subset G$ has $|S| \ge \epsilon n^{1/2}$, and that for each $h \neq 0$, $S$ contains at most $C$ pairs of the form $(x, x+h)$. If $t$ denotes any integer strictly larger than $\max(C, 1)$, this implies that $S^{2 \times t}$ contains no matrix of the form
\[
    \begin{pmatrix}
        x_1 & x_2 & \cdots & x_t \\
        x_1 + h & x_2 + h & \cdots & x_t + h
    \end{pmatrix},
\]
where $x_1, \ldots, x_t$ are distinct. In other words, $S$ is $(2, t)$-Sidon.

The conclusion would now follow from \cref{cor:linear-patterns-st-Sidon}, using $s = 2$ and $q = 4$, provided that we can show that
\[
    ||\widehat{\mathbbm{1}_S}||_4 \ll_{\epsilon,C} |S|.
\]
This is equivalent to a bound for the \emph{additive energy} of $S$:
\begin{equation} \label{eq:additive-energy}
    \#\left\{(a, b, c, d) \in S^4 : a - b = c - d \right\} \ll_{\epsilon,C} \frac{|S|^4}{n}.
\end{equation}
But we have 
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \#\left\{(a, b, c, d) \in S^4 : a - b = c - d \right\}
    &=
    \sum_{h \in G} \#\left\{(a, b, c, d) \in S^4 : a - b = c - d = h\right\}
    \\
    &=
    \sum_{h \in G} \left(\#\left\{(a, b) \in S^2 : a - b = h \right\}\right)^2.
\end{aligned}
\]
The contribution of $h = 0$ is exactly $|S|^2$. Moreover, by our second assumption, the contribution of each $h \neq 0$ is at most $C^2$. Overall, we obtain
\[
    \#\left\{(a, b, c, d) \in S^4 : a - b = c - d \right\} \le |S|^2 + C^2 n,
\]
which is acceptable in \cref{eq:additive-energy} since $|S| \ge \epsilon n^{1/2}$. This completes our proof.

nodes.statement: We start by proving a couple of claims about any linear function lambda(z) = az + b, with a, b in C: item[(a).] Given any (bounded) line segment S subset C, the maximum max_z in S |lambda(z)| is attained at one of the ends of S. item[(b).] Given any z_0 in C, there exists z_1 in \0\ cup \2^k, i2^k, -2^k, -i2^k : k in Z_ge 0\ such that |z_1| le max(1, 2sqrt2|z_0|), and |lambda(z_1)| ge |lambda(z_0)|. Claim (a) follows by writing S = \ct + d : t in [0, 1]\ for some c, d in C, and expressing |lambda(ct+d)|^2 as a convex function of t. For claim (b), draw a line segment through z_0 with slope in \pm 1\, intersecting both semi-axes of z_0's quadrant at w_1 and w_2 (if z_0 is purely real or imaginary, we may ignore this step). By claim (a), we must have |lambda(z_0)| le |lambda(w_i)| for some i in \1, 2\. Then, draw a line segment between 0 and 2^k w_i/|w_i|, where k ge 0 is minimal such that |w_i| le 2^k, and apply claim (a) again. Hence we can apply claim (b) to modify each of these values (g(x) for x in X and h(y) for y in Y, one at a time), while not decreasing the value of |E_x,y[f(x,y)g(x)h(y)]|, until the resulting functions g' and h' only have values in \0\ cup \2^k, i2^k, -2^k, -i2^k : k in Z_ge 0\. Then we have \[ leftvert E_x,y[f(x,y)g(x)h(y)] rightvert le leftvert E_x,y[f(x,y)g'(x)h'(y)] rightvert, \] \[ ||g'||_L^2^2 = E_xleft[ |g'(x)|^2 right] &le E_x left[1 + left(2sqrt2|g(x)|right)^2right] = 1 + 8||g||_L^2^2 = 9, \] and similarly ||h'||_L^2 le 3. The desired bound for ||f||_S^infty follows after taking a supremum over g, h, g', h'. Finally, to establish the entropy bounds for g and h, let g : X to \0\ cup \2^k, i2^k, -2^k, -i2^k : k in Z_ge 0\ have ||g||_L^2 le 3. Denoting by P_X(g = 0) the probability of the set \g = 0\ = g^-1(0), we have \[ H(g) = P_X(g = 0) log frac1P_X(g = 0) + sum_k=0^infty sum_omega^4 = 1 P_X(g = omega 2^k) log frac1P_X(g = omega 2^k), \] and \[ 9 ge ||g||_L^2^2 = sum_k=0^infty sum_omega^4 = 1 4^k P_X(g = omega 2^k). \] In particular, it follows that P_X(g = omega 2^k) le 9/4^k. nodes.name: Weighted version of \cref{thm:super-dense-removal}
nodes.statement: For any graph H, q in [1, 2), C > 0 and epsilon in (0, 1), there exists \[ delta ge exp left( - O_H,q,Cleft( epsilon^-O_H,q(1)right) right) \] such that the following holds. Let f : X times X to [0, infty) be a symmetric function (i.e., f(x, y) = f(y, x)) satisfying ||f||_L^infty le 1, ||f||_S^q le C, and E prod_\u, v\ in E(H) f(x_u, x_v) le delta. Then there is a symmetric set E subset X times X such that ||f mathbbm1_E^c||_L^1 le epsilon and prod_\u, v\ in E(H) mathbbm1_E(x_u, x_v) = 0 for any choice of the variables (x_u)_u in V(H).

nodes.raw_latex:
Note that $E(H)$ cannot be empty, since $\mathbf{E}[1] = 1 > \epsilon$. 

Let us apply our regularity lemma, \cref{thm:regularity}, for some parameter $\tau \in (0, 1)$ to be chosen later in the proof (in place of $\varepsilon$), the function $f$, and $r = 2$. This yields a partition $\mathcal{P}$ of $X$ with 
\[
    \mathbf{H}(\mathcal{P}) \le \frac{c(q)}{\tau^{4/(2-q)}},
\]
for some constant $c(q) > 0$, such that
\[
    ||f - \mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P} \otimes \mathcal{P})||_{L^2} \le \tau C.
\]
For brevity, we write $f_1 := \mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P} \otimes \mathcal{P})$ and $f_2 := f - f_1$, so that $f_1$ is $(\mathcal{P} \otimes \mathcal{P})$-measurable and $||f_2||_{L^2} \le \tau C$. Note that this has the effect of a \emph{strong} regularity lemma, but with no uniform component $f_3$ (and no tower-exponential dependencies).

We define $E^c \subset X \times X$ as the union of the following subsets $A \times B \in \mathcal{P} \otimes \mathcal{P}$, using three parameters $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ to be chosen later:
\begin{itemize}
    \item[$(i)$.] Those where $f_1$ is small (more precisely, smaller than $\alpha$);
    \item[$(ii)$.] Those where $|f_2|$ is large on average (more precisely, where $\mathbf{E}[|f_2| \mid A \times B] \ge \beta$);
    \item[$(iii)$.] Those with small probability (more precisely, with $\mathbf{P}(A) \le \gamma$ or $\mathbf{P}(B) \le \gamma$).
\end{itemize}
In other words, we defined $E$ by removing the blocks of edges above from $X \times X$. Now suppose for the sake of contradiction that $\prod_{\{u, v\} \in E(H)} \mathbbm{1}_E(x_u, x_v)$ is nonzero for some choice of $(x_u)_{u \in V(H)}$. Letting $A_u$ be the part of $\mathcal{P}$ containing $x_u$, we must have
\[
    (A_u, A_v) \in E,
    \qquad
    \forall \{u, v\} \in E(H).
\]
Assuming that \cref{eq:weighted-H-count} holds for some $\delta \in (0, 1)$ to be chosen later, we have
\[
    \mathbf{E} \left[ \prod_{w \in V(H)} \mathbbm{1}_{A_w}(x_w) \prod_{\{u, v\} \in E(H)} f(x_u, x_v) \right] \le \delta,
\]
and we may split $f = f_1 + f_2$ in each factor from the product above. In the resulting expansion, each term containing some instance of $f_2(x_u, x_v)$ is bounded, due to the $L^\infty$ bound on $f$, by
\[
\begin{aligned}
     \mathbf{E} \left[ |f_2|(x_u, x_v) \prod_{w \in V(H)} \mathbbm{1}_{A_w}(x_w) \right]
     &=
     \mathbf{E} \left[ \mathbf{E}(|f_2| \mid \mathcal{P} \otimes \mathcal{P})(x_u, x_v) \prod_{w \in V(H)} \mathbbm{1}_{A_w}(x_w) \right]
     \\
     &=
     \mathbf{E} \left[ \mathbf{E}[|f_2| \mid A_u \times A_v] \prod_{w \in V(H)} \mathbbm{1}_{A_w}(x_w) \right]
     \\
     &\le 
     \beta \prod_{w \in V(H)} \mathbf{P}(A_w).
\end{aligned}
\]
On the other hand, the term consisting only of $f_1$'s is lower-bounded, due to the removal of the type-$(i)$ blocks, by
\[
    \alpha^{|E(H)|} \prod_{w \in V(H)} \mathbf{P}(A_w).
\]
Putting the last three bounds together, we obtain $\left(\alpha^{|E(H)|} - \beta \right) \prod_{w \in V(H)} \mathbf{P}(A_w) \le \delta$, 
and we now choose $\beta := \alpha^{|E(H)|}/2$ to conclude that
\[
    \delta \ge \frac{\alpha^{|E(H)|}}{2} \prod_{w \in V(H)} \mathbf{P}(A_w)
    \ge 
    \frac{\alpha^{|E(H)|} \gamma^{|V(H)|}}{2}.
\]
Finally, we set 
\begin{equation} \label{eq:delta-choice}
    \delta := \frac{\alpha^{|E(H)|} \gamma^{|V(H)|}}{4}
\end{equation}
to obtain a contradiction (proving that $\prod_{\{u, v\} \in E(H)} \mathbbm{1}_E(x_u, x_v)$ is zero everywhere). It remains to choose suitable values for $\tau, \alpha, \gamma$ such that $||f \mathbbm{1}_{E^c}||_{L^1} \le \epsilon$. By the definition of $E^c$,
\[
    ||f \mathbbm{1}_{E^c}||_{L^1}
    \le
    \mathbf{E}[f \mathbbm{1}_{f_1 \le \alpha}]
    +
    \mathbf{P}(\mathbf{E}(|f_2| \mid \mathcal{P} \otimes \mathcal{P}) \ge \beta)
    +
    \mathbf{P}(R_\gamma)^2,
\]
where $R_\gamma$ denotes the union of all sets $A \in \mathcal{P}$ with $\mathbf{P}(A) \le \gamma$. But by the same reasoning as in \cref{eq:entropy-bound}, we have
\[
    \mathbf{P}(R_\gamma) \le \frac{\mathbf{H}(\mathcal{P})}{\log(1/\gamma)}
    \le 
    \frac{c(q)}{\tau^{4/(2-q)} \log(1/\gamma)}.
\]
At the same time, we have $\mathbf{E}[f \mathbbm{1}_{f_1 \le \alpha}] = \mathbf{E}[f_1 \mathbbm{1}_{f_1 \le \alpha}] \le \alpha$ and
\[
    \mathbf{P}(\mathbf{E}(|f_2| \mid \mathcal{P} \otimes \mathcal{P}) \ge \beta)
    \le 
    \frac{||f_2||_{L^1}}{\beta} 
    \le 
    \frac{2||f_2||_{L^2}}{\alpha^{|E(H)|}}
    \le 
    \frac{2\tau C}{\alpha^{|E(H)|}},
\]
so it makes sense to pick 
\[
    \alpha(\tau) := \tau^{1/2|E(H)|}
    \qquad\quad 
    \text{and} 
    \qquad\quad 
    \gamma(\tau) := \exp \left( - \frac{1}{\tau^{1+4/(2-q)}} \right),
\]
to conclude that 
\[
    ||f\mathbbm{1}_{E^c}||_{L^1} 
    \le 
    \tau^{1/2|E(H)|} + 2C \sqrt{\tau} + 
    c(q)^2 \tau^2.
\]
To ensure that the right-hand side is at most equal to $\epsilon$ (and that $\tau \in (0, 1)$), it suffices to pick some
\[
    \tau = \left(\frac{\epsilon}{O_{C,q}(1)}\right)^{2 E(H)}.
\]
Noting that both $\alpha(\tau)$ and $\gamma(\tau)$ are increasing functions of $\tau$, this produces (due to \cref{eq:delta-choice}) a value of
\[
    \delta 
    \gg 
    \exp \left(- \left(\frac{\epsilon}{O_{C,q}(1)}\right)^{-O_{H,q}(1)} \right)^{O_H(1)},
\]
as we wanted.

nodes.name: Relative logarithmic energy
nodes.statement: Let (X, P) be a finite probability space (with full sigma-algebra), P be a partition of X, and f, nu : X to [0, infty) satisfy f = 0 whenever nu = 0. Let us normalize f, nu such that E[f] = E[nu] = 1. We define the relative logarithmic energy of P with respect to f and nu by \[ E_f^nu(P) := E left[f log fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P) right], \] where we interpret ratios of 0/0 as 0. Note that the trivial partition has energy 0.

Let $(X, \mathbf{P})$ be a finite probability space (with full $\sigma$-algebra), $\mathcal{P}$ be a partition of $X$, and $f, \nu : X \to [0, \infty)$ satisfy $f = 0$ whenever $\nu = 0$. Let us normalize $f, \nu$ such that $\mathbf{E}[f] = \mathbf{E}[\nu] = 1$. We define the \emph{relative logarithmic energy} of $\mathcal{P}$ with respect to $f$ and $\nu$ by
\[
    \mathcal{E}_f^\nu(\mathcal{P}) := 
    \mathbf{E} \left[f \log \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})} \right],
\]
where we interpret ratios of $0/0$ as $0$. Note that the trivial partition has energy $0$.

\label{lem:logarithmic-energy-increment}
Let $\mathcal{P}, \mathcal{P}'$ be partitions of a finite probability space $(X, \mathbf{P})$ such that $\mathcal{P}'$ is finer than $\mathcal{P}$. Then one has
\[
    \mathbf{E} \left\vert \mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P}') - \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})} \mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P}') \right\vert 
    \le \sqrt{2\left(\mathcal{E}_f^\nu(\mathcal{P}') - \mathcal{E}_f^\nu(\mathcal{P})\right)}.
\]
In particular, this shows that relative logarithmic energy is nondecreasing and nonnegative.

nodes.name: Weak relative regularity lemma
nodes.statement: Let (X_1 times X_2, P) be a finite probability space, varepsilon in (0, 1), and f, nu : X_1 times X_2 to [0, infty) be such that f = 0 whenever nu = 0, and E[f] = E[nu] = 1. Then there is a partition P = P_1 otimes P_2 of X_1 times X_2 with 2^O(1/varepsilon^2) parts, such that \[ leftvert leftvert f - fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P)nurightvertrightvert_substack \\ square le varepsilon sqrtEleft[f log fracfnuright]. \] If X_1 = X_2, one can also take P_1 = P_2. In particular, if G is a finite graph with edge density p = E[mathbbm1_G] (allowing self-edges), one can find a partition P_0 of V(G) with 2^O(1/varepsilon^2) parts such that \[ leftvertleftvert mathbbm1_G - E(mathbbm1_G mid P_0 otimes P_0)rightvertrightvert_substack \\ square le varepsilon p sqrtlog(1/p), \] where P = P_0 otimes P_0. This last bound is sharp, in the sense that one cannot replace p sqrtlog(1/p) with a function of the form o_p to 0(p sqrtlog(1/p)) in the right-hand side, uniformly in G and varepsilon.

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{thm:weak-relative-regularity}
Let $(X_1 \times X_2, \mathbf{P})$ be a finite probability space, $\varepsilon \in (0, 1)$, and $f, \nu : X_1 \times X_2 \to [0, \infty)$ be such that $f = 0$ whenever $\nu = 0$, and $\mathbf{E}[f] = \mathbf{E}[\nu] = 1$. Then there is a partition $\mathcal{P} = \mathcal{P}_1 \otimes \mathcal{P}_2$ of $X_1 \times X_2$ with $2^{O(1/\varepsilon^2)}$ parts, such that
\[
    \left\vert \left\vert f - \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})}\nu\right\vert\right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}} \le \varepsilon \sqrt{\mathbf{E}\left[f \log \frac{f}{\nu}\right]}.
\]
If $X_1 = X_2$, one can also take $\mathcal{P}_1 = \mathcal{P}_2$. In particular, if $G$ is a finite graph with edge density $p = \mathbf{E}[\mathbbm{1}_G]$ (allowing self-edges), one can find a partition $\mathcal{P}_0$ of $V(G)$ with $2^{O(1/\varepsilon^2)}$ parts such that
\[
    \left\vert\left\vert \mathbbm{1}_{G} - \mathbf{E}(\mathbbm{1}_{G} \mid \mathcal{P}_0 \otimes \mathcal{P}_0)\right\vert\right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}} \le \varepsilon p \sqrt{\log(1/p)},
\]
where $\mathcal{P} = \mathcal{P}_0 \otimes \mathcal{P}_0$. This last bound is sharp, in the sense that one cannot replace $p \sqrt{\log(1/p)}$ with a function of the form $o_{p \to 0}(p \sqrt{\log(1/p)})$ in the right-hand side, uniformly in $G$ and $\varepsilon$.

Then there is a partition P = P_1 otimes P_2 of X_1 times X_2 with 2^O(1/varepsilon^2) parts, such that \[ leftvert leftvert f - fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P)nurightvertrightvert_substack \\ square le varepsilon sqrtEleft[f log fracfnuright]. \] If X_1 = X_2, one can also take P_1 = P_2. In particular, if G is a finite graph with edge density p = E[mathbbm1_G] (allowing self-edges), one can find a partition P_0 of V(G) with 2^O(1/varepsilon^2) parts such that \[ leftvertleftvert mathbbm1_G - E(mathbbm1_G mid P_0 otimes P_0)rightvertrightvert_substack \\ square le varepsilon p sqrtlog(1/p), \] where P = P_0 otimes P_0. This last bound is sharp, in the sense that one cannot replace p sqrtlog(1/p) with a function of the form o_p to 0(p sqrtlog(1/p)) in the right-hand side, uniformly in G and varepsilon.

nodes.name: Proof of \cref{thm:weak-relative-regularity}
nodes.statement: Let P be the family of partitions of the form P_1 otimes P_2, where P_i is a partition of X_i. We apply creflem:energy-optimization for the family P, varepsilon^2/4 in place of varepsilon, the complexity function C(P) = log_2 |P|, and the energy function E_f^nu(P); this produces a partition P = P_1 otimes P_2 with at most 2^4/varepsilon^2 parts, such that \[ E_f^nu (P vee Q) - E_f^nu(P) le fracvarepsilon^22 Eleft[f log fracfnuright] log_2 |Q|, \] for any partition Q = Q_1 otimes Q_2 of X_1 times X_2. Now consider the cut norm \[ leftvert leftvert f - fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P)nurightvertrightvert_substack \\ square &= sup_A_i subset X_i leftvert E left[ f mathbbm1_A_1 times A_2 - fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P)nu mathbbm1_A_1 times A_2 right] rightvert. \] For fixed A_1 and A_2, let Q_1 := \A_1, A_1^c\, Q_2 := \A_2, A_2^c\ and Q := Q_1 otimes Q_2. Then by creflem:logarithmic-energy-increment, we have \[ leftvert E left[ f mathbbm1_A_1 times A_2 - fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P)nu mathbbm1_A_1 times A_2 right] rightvert &= leftvert E left[ E(f mid P vee Q) mathbbm1_A_1 times A_2 - fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P)E(nu mid P vee Q) mathbbm1_A_1 times A_2 right] rightvert \\ &le E leftvert E(f mid P vee Q) - fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P)E(nu mid P vee Q) rightvert \\ &le sqrt2left( E_f^nu (P vee Q) - E_f^nu(P) right) \\ &le sqrt2fracvarepsilon^24E left[f log fracfnu right] log_2 4, \] which is what we wanted. When X_1 = X_2, one can instead use the family P of partitions of the form P_0 otimes P_0, and make the necessary modifications to Q (i.e., take Q_0 := Q_1 vee Q_2 and Q := Q_0 otimes Q_0). The statement about graphs follows by letting X_1 = X_2 := V(G), equipping V(G) times V(G) with the uniform probability measure, and letting f := mathbbm1_G/p and nu equiv 1. Finally, let us show that for any constant C > 0, one cannot in general choose a partition P = P_0 otimes P_0, where P_0 contains at most 2^C/varepsilon^2 parts, such that \[ leftvertleftvert mathbbm1_G - E(mathbbm1_G mid P)rightvertrightvert_substack \\ square le varepsilon o_p to 0left(p sqrtlog(1/p)right) \] holds simultaneously for all varepsilon in (0, 1) and all finite graphs G (where p := E[mathbbm1_G]), allowing self-edges. Let n ge 1 be large, p := 1/n, and varepsilon := sqrtC/log_2 (n/2); we will construct a graph G = G_n on n vertices, with edge density p, such that \[ leftvertleftvert mathbbm1_G_n - E(mathbbm1_G_n mid P) rightvertrightvert_substack \\ square gg frac1n, \] for all P = P_0 otimes P_0 such that P_0 contains at most 2^C/varepsilon^2 = n/2 sets. This will complete our proof since \[ varepsilon p sqrtlog(1/p) = frac1n sqrtfracC log nlog_2(n/2) ll_C frac1n, \] and thus the ratio ||mathbbm1_G - E(mathbbm1_G mid P)||_substack \\ square / left(varepsilon p sqrtlog(1/p)right) does not vanish as n to infty (i.e., p searrow 0). The construction is simple, using the same example as in : take V(G) = \1, ldots, n\ and mathbbm1_G(a, b) = mathbbm1_a = b for a, b in V(G), so that G consists of n loops. Then any partition P_0 of V(G) containing at most n/2 sets can use at most n/2 singletons (trivially); if k_1, ldots, k_m ge 2 denote the sizes of the remaining sets A_1, ldots, A_m in P_0, we thus have \[ k_1 + ldots + k_m ge n - fracn2 = fracn2. \] Now consider a cut C subset V(G) which splits each A_i roughly in half; more precisely, choose C subset A_1 cup cdots cup A_m such that |C cap A_i| = lceil k_i/2 rceil for i in \1, ldots, m\. Then we have \[ leftvertleftvert mathbbm1_G_n - E(mathbbm1_G_n mid P) rightvertrightvert_substack \\ square &ge E left[ left( mathbbm1_G_n - E(mathbbm1_G_n mid P)right)mathbbm1_C times C right] \\ &= frac1n^2sum_i=1^m sum_a, b in C cap A_i left(mathbbm1_a=b - frack_ik_i^2right) \\ &= frac1n^2sum_i=1^m left(|C cap A_i| - frac|C cap A_i|^2k_i right) = frac1n^2sum_i=1^m leftlceil frack_i2 rightrceil left(1 - fraclceil k_i/2 rceilk_i right). \] Since each k_i ge 2, it is easy to check that lceil k_i/2 rceil/k_i le 2/3, and thus \[ leftvertleftvert mathbbm1_G_n - E(mathbbm1_G_n mid P) rightvertrightvert_substack \\ square gg frac1n^2 sum_i=1^m frack_i2 gg frac1n, \] which completes our proof.

    \left\vert \left\vert f - \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})}\nu\right\vert\right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}}
    &=
    \sup_{A_i \subset X_i} \left\vert \mathbf{E} \left[ f \mathbbm{1}_{A_1 \times A_2} - \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})}\nu \mathbbm{1}_{A_1 \times A_2} \right] \right\vert.
\end{aligned}
\]
For fixed $A_1$ and $A_2$, let $\mathcal{Q}_1 := \{A_1, A_1^c\}$, $\mathcal{Q}_2 := \{A_2, A_2^c\}$ and $\mathcal{Q} := \mathcal{Q}_1 \otimes \mathcal{Q}_2$. Then by \cref{lem:logarithmic-energy-increment}, we have
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \left\vert \mathbf{E} \left[ f \mathbbm{1}_{A_1 \times A_2} - \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})}\nu \mathbbm{1}_{A_1 \times A_2} \right] \right\vert
    &=
    \left\vert \mathbf{E} \left[ \mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P} \vee \mathcal{Q}) \mathbbm{1}_{A_1 \times A_2} - \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})}\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P} \vee \mathcal{Q}) \mathbbm{1}_{A_1 \times A_2} \right] \right\vert
    \\
    &\le 
    \mathbf{E} \left\vert 
    \mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P} \vee \mathcal{Q}) - \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})}\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P} \vee \mathcal{Q}) \right\vert
    \\
    &\le 
    \sqrt{2\left( \mathcal{E}_f^\nu (\mathcal{P} \vee \mathcal{Q}) - \mathcal{E}_f^\nu(\mathcal{P}) \right)}
    \\
    &\le
    \sqrt{2\frac{\varepsilon^2}{4}\mathbf{E} \left[f \log \frac{f}{\nu} \right] \log_2 4},
\end{aligned}
\]
which is what we wanted. When $X_1 = X_2$, one can instead use the family $\mathscr{P}$ of partitions of the form $\mathcal{P}_0 \otimes \mathcal{P}_0$, and make the necessary modifications to $\mathcal{Q}$ (i.e., take $\mathcal{Q}_0 := \mathcal{Q}_1 \vee \mathcal{Q}_2$ and $\mathcal{Q} := \mathcal{Q}_0 \otimes \mathcal{Q}_0$).

The statement about graphs follows by letting $X_1 = X_2 := V(G)$, equipping $V(G) \times V(G)$ with the uniform probability measure, and letting $f := \mathbbm{1}_G/p$ and $\nu \equiv 1$.


Finally, let us show that for any constant $C > 0$, one cannot in general choose a partition $\mathcal{P} = \mathcal{P}_0 \otimes \mathcal{P}_0$, where $\mathcal{P}_0$ contains at most $2^{C/\varepsilon^2}$ parts, such that 
\[
    \left\vert\left\vert \mathbbm{1}_G - \mathbf{E}(\mathbbm{1}_G \mid \mathcal{P})\right\vert\right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}} \le \varepsilon o_{p \to 0}\left(p \sqrt{\log(1/p)}\right)
\]
holds simultaneously for all $\varepsilon \in (0, 1)$ and all finite graphs $G$ (where $p := \mathbf{E}[\mathbbm{1}_G]$), allowing self-edges. Let $n \ge 1$ be large, $p := 1/n$, and $\varepsilon := \sqrt{C/\log_2 (n/2)}$; we will construct a graph $G = G_n$ on $n$ vertices, with edge density $p$, such that
\[
    \left\vert\left\vert \mathbbm{1}_{G_n} - \mathbf{E}(\mathbbm{1}_{G_n} \mid \mathcal{P}) \right\vert\right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}} \gg 
    \frac{1}{n},
\]
for all $\mathcal{P} = \mathcal{P}_0 \otimes \mathcal{P}_0$ such that $\mathcal{P}_0$ contains at most $2^{C/\varepsilon^2} = n/2$ sets. This will complete our proof since 
\[
    \varepsilon p \sqrt{\log(1/p)} = \frac{1}{n} \sqrt{\frac{C \log n}{\log_2(n/2)}} 
    \ll_C 
    \frac{1}{n},
\]
and thus the ratio $||\mathbbm{1}_G - \mathbf{E}(\mathbbm{1}_G \mid \mathcal{P})||_{\substack{ \\ \square}} / \left(\varepsilon p \sqrt{\log(1/p)}\right)$ does not vanish as $n \to \infty$ (i.e., $p \searrow 0$).

The construction is simple, using the same example as in \cite[below Theorem 2.2]{conlon2021regularity}: take $V(G) = \{1, \ldots, n\}$ and $\mathbbm{1}_G(a, b) = \mathbbm{1}_{a = b}$ for $a, b \in V(G)$, so that $G$ consists of $n$ loops. Then any partition $\mathcal{P}_0$ of $V(G)$ containing at most $n/2$ sets can use at most $n/2$ singletons (trivially); if $k_1, \ldots, k_m \ge 2$ denote the sizes of the remaining sets $A_1, \ldots, A_m$ in $\mathcal{P}_0$, we thus have
\[
    k_1 + \ldots + k_m \ge n - \frac{n}{2} = \frac{n}{2}.
\]
Now consider a cut $C \subset V(G)$ which splits each $A_i$ roughly in half; more precisely, choose $C \subset A_1 \cup \cdots \cup A_m$ such that $|C \cap A_i| = \lceil k_i/2 \rceil$ for $i \in \{1, \ldots, m\}$. Then we have 
\[
\begin{aligned}
    \left\vert\left\vert \mathbbm{1}_{G_n} - \mathbf{E}(\mathbbm{1}_{G_n} \mid \mathcal{P}) \right\vert\right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}}
    &\ge 
    \mathbf{E} \left[ \left( \mathbbm{1}_{G_n} - \mathbf{E}(\mathbbm{1}_{G_n} \mid \mathcal{P})\right)\mathbbm{1}_{C \times C} \right]
    \\
    &=
    \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^m \sum_{a, b \in C \cap A_i} \left(\mathbbm{1}_{a=b} - \frac{k_i}{k_i^2}\right)
    \\
    &=
    \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^m \left(|C \cap A_i| - \frac{|C \cap A_i|^2}{k_i} \right)
    =
    \frac{1}{n^2}\sum_{i=1}^m \left\lceil \frac{k_i}{2} \right\rceil \left(1 - \frac{\lceil k_i/2 \rceil}{k_i} \right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since each $k_i \ge 2$, it is easy to check that $\lceil k_i/2 \rceil/k_i \le 2/3$, and thus
\[
    \left\vert\left\vert \mathbbm{1}_{G_n} - \mathbf{E}(\mathbbm{1}_{G_n} \mid \mathcal{P}) \right\vert\right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}}
    \gg \frac{1}{n^2} \sum_{i=1}^m \frac{k_i}{2} \gg \frac{1}{n},
\]
which completes our proof.

Then by crefthm:weak-relative-regularity, for any tau in (0, 1), there exists a partition P = P_1 otimes P_2 of X_1 times X_2 with 2^O(1/tau^2) parts such that \[ leftvert leftvert g - fracE(g mid P)E(mu mid P) mu rightvert rightvert_substack \\ square le tau sqrtEleft[g log fracgmu right]. \] Renormalizing and using the inequality f le mu E[nu], this translates to \[ leftvert leftvert f - fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P) nu rightvert rightvert_substack \\ square le delta tau sqrtEleft[fracfdelta log fracfdelta mu right] le delta tau sqrtlog fracE[nu]delta. \] On the other hand, since E(f mid P) le E(nu mid P), one can obtain the inequality \[ leftvert leftvert fracE(f mid P)E(nu mid P) (nu - 1) rightvert rightvert_substack \\ square le 2^O(1/tau^2) ||nu - 1||_substack \\ square, \] by expanding the right-hand side as a sum of 2^O(1/tau^2) terms (corresponding to the parts of P_1 otimes P_2). Putting the last two inequalities together and assuming that ||nu - 1||_substack \\ square le varepsilon' (for some varepsilon' > 0 to be chosen), we get that \[ ||f - widetildef||_substack \\ square le 2^O(1/tau^2) varepsilon' + delta tau sqrtlog fracE[nu]delta, \] where widetildef := E(f mid P)/E(nu mid P) le 1. The conclusion follows by choosing tau and then varepsilon' small enough such that each of the above terms is at most varepsilon/2.

If $f \equiv 0$, there is nothing to prove; taking $\varepsilon' < 1/2$, we can also guarantee that $\mathbf{E}[\nu] \asymp 1$. So let $\delta := \mathbf{E}[f] > 0$, $g := f/\delta$, and $\mu := \nu/\mathbf{E}[\nu]$. Then by \cref{thm:weak-relative-regularity}, for any $\tau \in (0, 1)$, there exists a partition $\mathcal{P} = \mathcal{P}_1 \otimes \mathcal{P}_2$ of $X_1 \times X_2$ with $2^{O(1/\tau^2)}$ parts such that 
\[
    \left\vert \left\vert 
    g - \frac{\mathbf{E}(g \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\mu \mid \mathcal{P})} \mu 
    \right\vert \right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}} 
    \le 
    \tau \sqrt{\mathbf{E}\left[g \log \frac{g}{\mu} \right]}.
\]
Renormalizing and using the inequality $f \le \mu \mathbf{E}[\nu]$, this translates to
\[
    \left\vert \left\vert 
    f - \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})} \nu 
    \right\vert \right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}} 
    \le 
    \delta \tau \sqrt{\mathbf{E}\left[\frac{f}{\delta} \log \frac{f}{\delta \mu} \right]}
    \le 
    \delta \tau \sqrt{\log \frac{\mathbf{E}[\nu]}{\delta}}.
\]
On the other hand, since $\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P}) \le \mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})$, one can obtain the inequality
\[
    \left\vert \left\vert 
    \frac{\mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})}{\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P})} (\nu - 1) 
    \right\vert \right\vert_{\substack{ \\ \square}} 
    \le 
    2^{O(1/\tau^2)}
    ||\nu - 1||_{\substack{ \\ \square}},
\]
by expanding the right-hand side as a sum of $2^{O(1/\tau^2)}$ terms (corresponding to the parts of $\mathcal{P}_1 \otimes \mathcal{P}_2$).

Putting the last two inequalities together and assuming that $||\nu - 1||_{\substack{ \\ \square}} \le \varepsilon'$ (for some $\varepsilon' > 0$ to be chosen), we get that
\[
    ||f - \widetilde{f}||_{\substack{ \\ \square}} 
    \le 
    2^{O(1/\tau^2)} \varepsilon' + \delta \tau \sqrt{\log \frac{\mathbf{E}[\nu]}{\delta}},
\]
where $\widetilde{f} := \mathbf{E}(f \mid \mathcal{P})/\mathbf{E}(\nu \mid \mathcal{P}) \le 1$. The conclusion follows by choosing $\tau$ and then $\varepsilon'$ small enough such that each of the above terms is at most $\varepsilon/2$.
